facts.text: Longfellow takes its name from poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, whose poem “The Song of Hiawatha” weaves stories of the Dakota people who once lived here.
The neighborhood’s streets are lined with Craftsman‑style homes and the famous Minnehaha Mile, a bike‑friendly boulevard full of vintage and secondhand shops.
Minnehaha Falls, an urban waterfall that changes with the seasons, sits in the heart of Longfellow’s parkland and is a favorite spot for locals and visitors alike.
Every summer night, residents hear mysterious booms that have been described as house‑shakingly loud, a phenomenon that has puzzled scientists and police for decades.
Investigations into the booms have ruled out fireworks, train decoupling, and even secret military flights, leaving the cause still unexplained.
In 2026, a new hum was traced to industrial fans atop the renovated Atkinson grain mill on East 38th Street and Hiawatha Avenue, showing how modern industry can shape local soundscapes.
